channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: O que Sergio Moro achou da fala de Milei sobre Lula
item.description: Sergio Moro defended Javier Milei's remarks against Lula and Alexandre de Moraes, stating they should be understood in the context of political reciprocity and the emotional atmosphere of party conventions. He emphasized that Milei's economic achievements — such as reducing bureaucracy, controlling public spending, and Argentina's economic recovery — outweigh the controversy. Moro also said he aims to apply similar principles in a potential government of Paraná.

item.title: PL busca vice para Flávio Bolsonaro enquanto prepara convenção partidária no DF
item.description: The Liberal Party is intensifying internal negotiations to select a running mate for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 presidential race. This effort coincides with preparations for the party's convention in the Federal District, which will formalize the ticket. The move reflects the PL's strategy to solidify its bolsonarist-aligned base ahead of the next election.

item.title: Democratas acusam governo Trump de conspirar contra eleições no Brasil
item.description: Democratic senators from the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee accused the Trump administration of spreading conspiracy theories about Brazil’s 2026 presidential elections, arguing it undermines U.S. democracy and alienates international allies. The accusation followed the denial of visas by Itamaraty to two Trump administration officials allegedly planning to travel to Brasília to challenge the integrity of Brazil’s electoral system — a claim the Trump administration labeled as baseless. The allegations come amid Trump’s public support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, and after diplomatic tensions arose from Argentine President Javier Milei’s visit to Brazil, where he criticized Lula and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Sergio Moro: ‘Nós temos um adversário em comum, o Bolsonaro e eu’
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) stated that he and Jair Bolsonaro share a common adversary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, whose administration he describes as an 'economic and moral tragedy'. Moro announced his support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential candidacy and reiterated his own pre-candidacy for governor of Paraná, focusing on anti-corruption, health, education, infrastructure, and reducing the state tax burden, aiming to make Paraná 'the Texas of Brazil'.

item.title: Milei faz desserviço à Argentina ao criticar Lula, diz Alckmin
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin criticized Argentine President Javier Milei for making negative statements about Brazilian President Lula, saying Milei did a disservice to Argentina by attacking its largest trading partner. Milei's remarks, made at a PL event in São Paulo, included insults toward Brazilian officials and heightened tensions between the two countries, prompting Brazil to summon ambassadors for consultations and formal protests. Alckmin also emphasized strengthening Brazil-South Korea relations, aiming to double bilateral trade within two years.

item.title: Derrite comenta especulação sobre desistência do Senado
item.description: Federal deputy Guilherme Derrite (PL) denied being pressured by the PP to withdraw from the Senate race, calling reports of his potential withdrawal to make room for Paulinho da Força (Solidariedade) false. He reaffirmed his commitment to the Senate campaign on Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' (Republicanos) ticket.

item.title: Diretor da OMS diz que Brasil é exemplo mundial por sistema de saúde
item.description: The WHO Director-General, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, praised Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) as a global example of universal coverage, serving over 200 million people. He highlighted Brazil's progress in eliminating mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B and the long-standing cooperation between WHO and institutions like Fiocruz. President Lula emphasized that the SUS succeeds due to the dedication of all health workers.

item.title: EUA voltam a falar em “perseguição” contra Bolsonaro e citam STF
item.description: The U.S. government under Donald Trump renewed the national emergency against Brazil, claiming political persecution of Jair Bolsonaro and his family by the Lula government, as well as alleged censorship by the Supreme Federal Court. Although symbolic and imposing no new sanctions, the measure was justified as a response to an extraordinary threat to U.S. national security, foreign policy, and economy originating in Brazil. The renewal extends Executive Order 14323 from July 2025 for another year.

item.title: TSE firma parcerias com plataformas digitais para as eleições de 2026
item.description: The TSE has formalized partnerships with digital platforms including Facebook, Google, Kwai, TikTok, LinkedIn, X and Telegram to combat disinformation in the 2026 elections. The agreements include reporting channels, staff training, direct voter communication tools (such as Megafone and WhatsApp Business API), access to Meta’s Ad Library, and protection against cyberattacks via Project Shield. These initiatives are part of the Permanent Program to Combat Electoral Disinformation by the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Michelle confirma presença em convenção do PL em Brasília
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro confirmed her attendance at the PL party convention in the Federal District to formalize the party's candidates on August 2, 2026, with her Senate candidacy nearly finalized. The event will mark her first public appearance with Flávio Bolsonaro since their public rift over electoral alliances, though he has not yet confirmed his presence. Despite Flávio's apology on July 23, Michelle did not attend the party's national convention in São Paulo on July 25, sending only a four-minute video instead.

item.title: Alckmin repudia falas de Milei sobre Lula: “Absolutamente grosseiras”
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) denounced remarks by Argentine President Javier Milei about Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, calling them 'absolutely gross' and lamenting that a leader of a neighboring friendly country had done a disservice to his nation. Milei’s comments were made during the PL National Convention on Saturday, the 25th.

item.title: Governo prorroga Desenrola até 31 de agosto
item.description: The government extended the Desenrola Brasil debt renegotiation program until August 31, maintaining original conditions without additional fiscal impact on the Union, according to Finance Minister Dario Durigan. The extension aims to allow more people to complete debt renegotiations, with a goal of reaching 10 million beneficiaries, and to facilitate access to vehicle fleet renewal programs.

item.title: Durante visita de Lula, Ricardo Couto anuncia apoio da União para ampliar atendimento no Hospital Pedro Ernesto
item.description: During President Lula's visit to the Federal Hospital of Andaraí, acting Governor Ricardo Couto announced that the Ministry of Health will support the expansion of care capacity at the Pedro Ernesto University Hospital, in response to a request from State Health Secretary Manoel Damião. The announcement was made during a ceremony presenting federal investments in Rio's hospital network, though Couto did not disclose funding amounts or timelines. The hospital had previously faced a crisis in early 2025 when it deactivated a 15-bed ICU due to budget constraints after pandemic-related funding ended.

item.title: A reação de Alckmin aos ataques de Milei a Lula e Moraes
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin condemned the offensive remarks made by Argentine President Javier Milei against Brazil, calling them a gross interference in internal affairs, particularly during the electoral period. He noted that Milei had insulted President Lula and Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, and emphasized Brazil's role as Argentina's main trading partner, without directly addressing potential impacts on bilateral relations.

item.title: Lula defende SUS e diz que Trump também seria tratado na rede pública
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended universal healthcare access through the SUS during a meeting with the WHO Director-General at the Federal Hospital of Andaraí in Rio. He stated that even leaders like Donald Trump would receive the same public treatment, emphasizing that healthcare should not depend on wealth. Lula stressed that the SUS provides care without requiring proof of income or employment and highlighted the recovery of Rio’s federal health network as a reversal of setbacks under Bolsonaro’s administration.

item.title: Sóstenes declara R$ 500 mil em espécie ao TSE
item.description: The leader of the PL in the Chamber of Deputies, Sóstenes Cavalcante, declared to the Electoral Justice that he holds R$ 500,000 in cash. Of this amount, R$ 468,000 was seized by the Federal Police in a December operation last year at an address linked to the parliamentarian. The declaration was submitted to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) as part of financial reporting.

item.title: Aliado de Flávio, Cleitinho anunciará candidatura em MG na próxima semana
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos-MG) is set to announce his candidacy for governor of Minas Gerais next week, following a delay due to the recent death of his brother Matheus in July. His endorsement of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for president is expected to bolster the conservative ticket in Brazil’s second-largest electoral college, with the Republicanos planning a pure slate featuring Luís Eduardo Falcão as vice-governor.

item.title: Lula cobra bancos públicos para destravar crédito do Move Aplicativos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged the heads of federal public banks to unlock credit access through the Move Aplicativos program, which finances new and used cars for ride-hailing drivers. The initiative aims to improve financial inclusion for this workforce, stimulate the automotive sector, and support income generation.

item.title: Patrimônio de Ricardo Salles mais que dobra e inclui imóvel rural em Portugal
item.description: Federal deputy Ricardo Salles (Novo), a Senate candidate in the 2026 elections, declared assets worth R$ 9.05 million to the Electoral Justice, a 128% increase from the R$ 3.97 million reported in 2022. The growth includes a rural property in Portugal, as stated in the asset declaration submitted to the TSE.

item.title: Alvo da PF, Sóstenes declara R$ 500 mil em dinheiro vivo ao TSE
item.description: Sóstenes Cavalcante (PL-RJ), running for re-election in 2026, declared to the TSE R$ 500,000 in cash and R$ 100,000 in land in Brasília, totaling R$ 600,000 in assets. The cash was claimed to come from a property sale, but in December the PF seized R$ 468,000 in cash at an address linked to him, investigating alleged misappropriation of parliamentary funds. His declared wealth marks a sharp increase from the R$ 4,426.76 reported in 2022.

item.title: Milei errou ao criticar Lula, diz ex-embaixador argentino
item.description: Former Argentine ambassador to Brazil Juan Pablo Lohlé criticized Javier Milei’s remarks against Lula, calling them disproportionate and damaging to Argentina, which lacks Brazil’s economic and diplomatic strength to withstand such tensions. He argued Argentina’s Foreign Ministry should have intervened to prevent the incident and deemed a Milei apology unlikely in the short term due to his ideological rigidity.

item.title: Caiado diz que Milei fez 'escândalo', mas critica governo Lula: 'Não se governa na esculhambação'
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Javier Milei for causing a 'scandal' by speaking at the PL convention and attacked the Lula government, stating that 'you cannot govern in chaos'. He advocated restoring the 'liturgic dignity' of the presidency and accused Itamaraty of losing autonomy, becoming an ideological arm of the Workers' Party.

item.title: Moraes dá 48h para Daniel Silveira explicar vídeo de apoio a candidato
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes gave Daniel Silveira's defense 48 hours to respond to allegations of violating judicial measures after the former deputy appeared in a video supporting Carlos Portinho's Senate candidacy. The case concerns alleged breach of restrictions imposed on Silveira due to his involvement in anti-democratic acts.

item.title: Senadores americanos falam de 'conspiração' contra eleição brasileira
item.description: Democratic senators on the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee accused the Trump administration of spreading conspiracy theories about Brazil's October presidential elections. They claim these allegations aim to undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process in the country.

item.title: Lula diz que 'elite nasce de costas para o morro e de frente para a praia'
item.description: President Lula criticized Brazil's elite for being unaware of poverty, stating they 'are born with their backs to the hill and facing the beach or the airport'. The remarks were made during a visit to the Federal Hospital of Andaraí in Rio de Janeiro, accompanied by WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom, as part of an event highlighting public health programs.

item.title: Lula presta solidariedade ao Japão após terremoto no sul do país
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva expressed solidarity with Japan following a 6.8-magnitude earthquake that struck Kumamoto Prefecture in the early hours of Tuesday (28/7). He offered support to the Japanese people, affected families, and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, referencing their recent meeting at the G7 Summit in Évian.

item.title: Caiado defende “tomar todos os bens” de agressor de mulheres
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado proposed confiscating all assets of men convicted of violence against women and transferring them to victims or their children in femicide cases, based on the legal institute of asset forfeiture. He argued the measure would break the cycle of financial dependence that keeps women in abusive relationships. Caiado also advocated for harsher penalties, including denying early release or regime progression until a minimum sentence is served.

item.title: Lula pede que diretor da OMS leve a Trump defesa de verbas para saúde pública
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva asked WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus to convey to U.S. President Donald Trump the importance of maintaining funding for the World Health Organization to ensure quality healthcare for the poorest populations. The request was made during an event at the Federal Hospital of Andaraí in Rio de Janeiro, where Lula emphasized the WHO's role in promoting global health equity.

item.title: Porta-voz de Milei minimiza ataques a Lula: “Houve insultos dos dois lados”
item.description: The spokesperson for the Argentine Presidency, Adrian Ravier, downplayed the diplomatic crisis between Brazil and Argentina, stating that insults came from both sides but that Argentina had never taken ideological differences to the diplomatic level. The remarks followed Argentine President Javier Milei’s attacks on Lula during a PL event in São Paulo, where he called the Brazilian president a 'thief', 'convict', and 'socialist trash', and encouraged supporters to chant 'Lula thief'.

item.title: Caiado sobre escolha de ministros do STF: “Não vale botar um amigo”
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized the appointment of personal friends to the Supreme Federal Court, stating that presidents should not nominate ministers based on personal loyalty or political interests. He argued that selections must prioritize impeccable reputation, legal expertise, and total independence, and expressed support for a STF reform to ensure greater impartiality in judicial appointments.

item.title: Alckmin diz que Milei presta desserviço à Argentina
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin criticized Argentine President Javier Milei for insulting President Lula and Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes during a PL party event in São Paulo, calling the remarks meddlesome and gross. He stressed that foreign leaders should not interfere in other countries’ elections and highlighted the strong trade ties between Brazil and Argentina, noting Brazil is Argentina’s largest trading partner.

item.title: Moraes nega recurso e mantém cassação de Arthur do Val, o Mamãe Falei
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a petition by former São Paulo state deputy Arthur do Val ('Mamãe Falei'), upholding his 2022 mandate cassation for breach of parliamentary decorum following sexist remarks about Ukrainian women in leaked WhatsApp audio. The defense sought annulment of the process, citing due process violations, but Moraes ruled the constitutional claim was inappropriate for reopening the case.

item.title: Lula presta solidariedade ao Japão após terremoto de magnitude 7,1 atingir o país
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva expressed solidarity with Japan after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture, injuring at least 50 people and collapsing 12 buildings. In a social media post, Lula conveyed his consternation and offered support to affected families and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, whom he met recently at the G7 Summit.

item.title: “Essa loucura chegou a proporções inimagináveis”, diz Caiado sobre 8/1
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado stated that, if elected, he would grant amnesty to those convicted for the anti-democratic acts of January 8 to 'pacify the country'. He criticized Lula's government diplomacy, accusing the Itamaraty of being 'a PT arm', and said Brazil cannot elect 'the most rejected', referring to Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Caiado also linked recent diplomatic crises to internal polarization, claiming other countries are using the January 8 case to divert attention from their own shortcomings.

item.title: Caiado critica diplomacia do governo Lula: "Itamaraty é um braço do PT”
item.description: PSD presidential candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized the Lula government's foreign policy, claiming Itamaraty is 'an arm of the PT' and pledged to restore Brazil's diplomacy through dialogue and national interests. He emphasized using Brazil's strategic assets — critical minerals, agribusiness, and renewable energy — as tools in international negotiations, rejecting public confrontations between heads of state.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula participa de reunião da Sociedade para o Progresso da Ciência
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the 78th Annual Meeting of the Brazilian Society for the Progress of Science (SBPC) in Niterói, RJ, on Tuesday, July 28, 2026. The event discusses science, technology, innovation, and education, bringing together researchers, authorities, and representatives from scientific institutions.

item.title: Caiado diz que Lula explodiu orçamento de 2027: “É o Dilma 2”
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) accused President Lula (PT) of having 'exploded' the 2027 budget with populist concessions, comparing the economic outlook to a 'Dilma 2' scenario with risks of 4 million unemployed and company closures. He advocated cutting parliamentary amendments, criticized Brazil’s declining international influence, and claimed to possess the 'moral stature' to earn the confidence of the business sector.

item.title: "Tarcísio é caiadista e Gilberto Kassab apoia a candidatura", diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado, PSD candidate for president in 2026, claims that São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas is a political ally ('caiadista') and that Gilberto Kassab, national president of the PSD, supports his candidacy. He emphasizes the PSD’s strong municipal structure as a key asset, highlighting its nationwide reach and Kassab’s political articulation skills. The remarks were made in a Metrópoles interview, shortly after Tarcísio attended the PL’s national convention in Brasília.

item.title: Mãe de Flávio Bolsonaro muda de plano e disputará vaga na Câmara
item.description: Rogeria Bolsonaro, mother of Flávio Bolsonaro and former Rio de Janeiro city councilwoman, will run for a federal deputy seat under the PL, abandoning her potential role as a Senate substitute. The decision comes amid uncertainty over the PL’s alliance with the União Progressista, following the arrest and release of Márcio Canella. Allies believe she can inherit part of the Bolsonaro electorate in Rio and strengthen the PL’s congressional bloc.

item.title: Líder do PL declara R$ 500 mil em espécie ao TSE enquanto PF investiga versão sobre R$ 468 mil apreendidos
item.description: The leader of the PL in the Chamber, Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ), declared R$ 500,000 in cash to the TSE, of which R$ 468,000 were seized by the Federal Police in December 2023. The PF is investigating whether the deputy's claim about the origin of the funds — allegedly from a property sale — is truthful, given evidence of fraud and attempts to conceal proof related to a scheme diverting parliamentary funds.

item.title: Lula alfineta Trump em fala a diretor da OMS: 'Como um país que não é rico como os EUA consegue garantir tratamento de saúde?'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized U.S. President Donald Trump for announcing cuts to World Health Organization (WHO) funding, highlighting that Brazil, despite not being as wealthy as the U.S., guarantees equal healthcare access through the Unified Health System (SUS). Lula made these remarks during a visit to the Federal Hospital of Andaraí in Rio de Janeiro, accompanied by WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, and stressed that healthcare access should not depend on income.

item.title: Lula reúne ministros para discutir desempenho de programa de crédito para taxistas e motoristas de aplicativos
item.description: President Lula met with ministers and public bank presidents to discuss the low approval rate of loans under the Move Brasil program for taxi and app drivers, despite R$30 billion being allocated, only R$3 billion has been disbursed since June. The government plans to pressure Febraban to ease credit access, viewing the program as an electoral strategy to boost his popularity ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Planalto avalia que Trump e Milei fazem dobradinha para tumultuar eleições no Brasil e ajudar Flávio
item.description: The Planalto believes Donald Trump and Javier Milei are coordinating a strategy to undermine Brazil's electoral system and benefit Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential candidacy, including blocking U.S. officials' entry and promoting false claims about electronic voting machine fraud.

item.title: Lula pede para diretor da OMS mandar recado sobre o SUS para Trump: ‘Saúde não é para rico’
item.description: President Lula asked the WHO Director-General, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, to deliver a message to U.S. President Donald Trump, emphasizing that Brazil's SUS provides equal healthcare access to all citizens, including cancer treatment for the poor, regardless of income. Lula stressed that health is not a privilege for the rich but a right for the sick, and advocated for preventive care to avoid unnecessary illness.

item.title: Advogados da União pedem direito a penduricalhos que TCU liberou para seus servidores
item.description: Lawyers from the Union have requested the same benefit granted by the TCU to its own employees, as well as to Senate and Chamber staff: payment of bonuses outside the constitutional spending cap. The TCU’s decision, approved by 8 votes to 1, went against its internal technical advice and the STF’s interpretation. The article is subscriber-only and concerns a matter that could influence broader debates on public sector compensation and equity.

item.title: Quando um sobrenome pode mudar a política brasileira
item.description: The book 'O Sobrenome — Bolsonaro depois de Bolsonaro' investigates whether the Bolsonaro surname could inaugurate Brazil’s first national political dynasty since redemocratization, analyzing the transfer of symbolic capital from Jair to Flávio Bolsonaro. Based on five months of interdisciplinary research, the work highlights the technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula in 2026 voting intentions as evidence of a break from Brazil’s tradition of lacking enduring national successors.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula não vai ao Peru para não ser visto como peça de museu
item.description: Lula chose not to travel to Peru for Keiko Fujimori's inauguration, avoiding being seen as a museum piece amid successive right-wing victories in Latin American regional elections. Instead of attending in person, he sent Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira as Brazil's representative.

item.title: Ricardo Salles declara R$ 9 milhões em bens, incluindo casa em Portugal
item.description: Ricardo Salles, former Environment Minister and Senate candidate for São Paulo, declared R$ 9 million in assets to the TSE, including a rural house in Portugal valued at R$ 3 million — a 127.95% increase from his 2022 declaration, when he reported approximately R$ 4 million in assets.

item.title: Líder do PL declara ao TSE ter 500 mil em dinheiro vivo, mas PF levou quase tudo
item.description: PL leader in the Chamber, Sóstenes Cavalcante, declared to the TSE that he held R$ 500,000 in cash from the sale of a property and a land valued at R$ 100,000. Nearly all of the cash amount (R$ 470,000) was seized by the Federal Police during Operation Galho Fraco in December last year. Cavalcante stated the money has legitimate origins and claimed he is a victim of judicial persecution.

item.title: Lula defende o SUS e alfineta Trump: "Saúde não é só para rico"
item.description: President Lula defended Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) during a visit to the Federal Hospital of Andaraí in Rio de Janeiro, criticizing Donald Trump's decision to cut WHO funding and asserting that healthcare access should not depend on financial status. He cited his own skin cancer treatment in the public system to illustrate that SUS provides equal care for rich and poor, emphasizing that 'healthcare treatment is not only for the rich'.
